scenes.headline: How SpatialScout grades an agent that maps a room
scenes.sub: A camera to drive, a list of objects, and one point per object
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ratline! SpatialScout drops an agent into a room it has never seen and asks for a map. Here's how that map is graded.

scenes.text: The agent never submits a box. It submits one 3D centre per object, and the scorer slides the true box onto that point and measures the overlap.
scenes.mark: slides the true box onto that point
scenes.say: The agent submits one centre per object. The scorer slides the true box onto that point and measures the overlap.

steps.say: The agent gets object IDs and categories, and one image. No positions.
It moves a calibrated camera and captures new views, up to a hundred.
For depth, it marks one feature in two views, and the tool intersects the rays.
It submits a centre per object, and revises as it explores.
Only afterwards does the scorer compare the map with the truth.

parts.note: box side minus the offset: what still overlaps
parts.say: Shift a box of side L by d, and L minus d still overlaps.

parts.note: the span the two boxes cover together
parts.say: Together they span L plus d.
So above zero point nine needs an offset under a nineteenth of the side. For a thin painting, a millimetre or two.

scenes.title: A ruler made of built maps
scenes.note: Ruler measured with the released scorer; Opus reported
scenes.say: I ran the released scorer on maps I built. Five centimetres of noise everywhere scores about thirty seven percent. The best agent scores about forty two.

scenes.title: How the failed runs failed

items.say: Most failed runs stopped before finding everything.

items.text: Rays met on the wrong spot
items.say: Many submitted a wrong point though the rays met cleanly.
Some kept points the tool had flagged.

scenes.say: The authors read forty runs. Six succeeded.

scenes.label: an exact map, same-group IDs swapped, in the released scorer
scenes.note: the paper says such swaps are free
scenes.say: One catch. In the released code, a perfect map with chairs filed under each other's IDs scores seventy nine percent.

scenes.text: A low triangulation residual proves the rays met. It does not prove they met on the object, or at its centre.
scenes.say: A low residual proves the rays met. Not that they met on the object's centre.

recap: Drive the camera, triangulate, submit centres
The true box slides onto each point
Best agent: a few centimetres off
scenes.say: Drive the camera and triangulate. The true box slides onto each point. The best agent lands a few centimetres off.
